text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Richard Holbrooke, the U.S. presidential emissary on the Cyprus problem, seeks a consensus among the "15" in Europe to follow such a policy on Cyprus so that the procedure to accession can be a catalyst in solving the conflict.

- Communist Akel and centre-left United Democrats meet today amid concerns that a tripartite pact may fall apart among opposition parties in fielding a common candidate in next year's presidential elections.

- Communist Akel general-secretary Demetris Christofias warns the United Democrats that procedures to approve a common opposition candidate must be concluded this month. The United Democrats will take a decision at the end of August.
- Russian mafia in Cyprus? No, says the intelligence service.
- Turkey and the pseudostate announced measures for "partial integration" in an attempt to blackmail the European Commission to back down on its decision to start entry talks with Cyprus next year.
- Paid killer is being sought for the murder of father of four from Limassol. His wife's lover is in custody for questioning.
- Bulent Ecevit and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash are promoting the integration of the occupied areas with Turkey, torpedoeing dialogue.
- The resumption of talks on Cyprus has injected a feeling of confidence in the development of Cyprus's economy, says Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou.
- Problems plague the cancer treatment unit for children in Nicosia. There is only one doctor who works 18 hours a day, while there is a shortage of auxiliary staff.
